note: THE RULES THIS ESTATE WRITES DOWN TWICE. Every entry names one rule that exists in more than one file - usually because a PowerShell lane and a Python lane must answer the same question - and the exact text to lift out of each side. audit-twin-drift.ps1 lifts them and fails when the copies stop matching. THIS FILE IS THE POINT: a twin nobody declared is a twin nobody is watching, which is how every drift in this estate's history got in. When you write a second implementation of an existing rule, add it here in the same commit.
history: Get-LinkPerUnit lived in two files and they disagreed on 13 of 3,342 links, the private copy wrong on every one. The price formatter had FIVE copies and three surfaces drifted. The notes-vs-bid check has two implementations that fire on disjoint refusal words. stated_mass_grams and Get-StatedMassGrams both dropped the whole number off a mixed fraction, reading '4 3/4 lb' as 340 g against 2154 g. RX_PROTEIN drifted from its PowerShell twin and read '47.3g protein' as 3g - caught by a hand-written LOCKSTEP case in a suite nothing ran, so it sat red for weeks. Not one of these was found by a check that was looking for it.

twins.name: prose-calorie-claim
twins.why: coverage_check's prose gate and spec-contradiction-lib both read a calorie claim out of recipe prose and compare it to the stat. If one is tightened and the other is not, the audit certifies a repair it does not describe.

twins.name: prose-protein-claim
twins.why: THE ONE THAT PROVED THE CLASS. The PowerShell side was fixed for decimals and the Python side was not, so `\b` sat between the '.' and the '3' of "47.3g protein" and the gate reported 'says 3g protein, stat says 47' against a CORRECT spec. Its own LOCKSTEP case caught it and nobody read the suite.

twins.name: prose-macro-claim
twins.why: THE TWIN THAT ONLY EVER EXISTED ON ONE SIDE, and three live cards paid for it. coverage_check.py has read carb and fat claims out of prose as RX_MACRO since the v3 gate, and said so in a comment: 'NO POWERSHELL TWIN: spec-contradiction-lib carries calorie and protein patterns only'. The Python half runs per-recipe before QA; the PowerShell half is what gates the whole CATALOGUE at publish - so the half that could see fat never looked at published recipes, and the half that looks at published recipes could not see fat. {{carbs}} and {{fat}} reached render-tokens on 2026-08-31, nothing swept the literals behind them, and bbq-chicken-rice-bowls shipped 'just 4 grams of fat' on a 10 g stat, hot-honey-chicken-bowls 3 on a 10, ground-beef-gyro-bowls 11 on a 13, each beside a stat block printing the true number on the same page. A missing twin is not a smaller version of a drifted twin; it is a rule that runs on a subset of its inputs and reports clean on the rest. Declared with the PowerShell side on 2026-09-01.

twins.name: deal-builder-size-token
twins.why: FOUND BY THIS AUDITOR'S OWN UNDECLARED SWEEP on its first run, 2026-09-01, which is the point of that sweep. The size-token parser that reads a quantity and unit out of a product NAME is byte-identical (139 chars, md5 d7854998dde1) in the Sam's and Walmart deal builders. Nothing was watching it. A unit added to one store's list and not the other's would silently mis-size every product carrying it at that store - and per-unit price is the number this whole estate publishes.

twins.name: stated-mass-number
twins.why: The number half of the mass reader that decides a recipe's MAIN PROTEIN weight. Both twins carried the identical mixed-fraction bug on 2026-09-01: the mixed alternative must LEAD, or a pattern wanting a unit after the digits cannot match '4 3/4 lb' from the front and the search slides on to '3/4 lb'. band_precheck uses the result, so reading low understates calories and can reject a sound recipe on the macro band.

twins.name: scaler-quantity-leadin
twins.why: The closed list of hedge words the serving scaler is allowed to look PAST when it hunts for a label's quantity. It exists in the browser (tpl2-scaler-prefix.html, which is what a reader actually runs) and in its PowerShell twin Invoke-CmScaleBuy, which is the only copy the repair scripts' fixtures can execute. Added 2026-09-01 with the widening itself: a word added to one side and not the other means the card and every self-test that claims to mirror it disagree about which labels scale, and the disagreement is invisible until a reader moves the servings control. The JS side is deliberately written as a regex LITERAL rather than a quoted string so the two texts are byte-comparable without normalising escapes.

twins.name: scaler-restatement-prefix
twins.why: The two prefixes the serving scaler may look past to find a quantity that is stated as a restatement rather than measured out: 'juice of' and 'zest of'. The 2026-09-01 widening refused both BY NAME, and for the general case that was right; on four live rows it is the only statement of the amount, so they were admitted to the LEAD path on 2026-09-03 (queue 2026-09-02-corn06). Declared in the same commit as the widening itself, because a prefix added to one side and not the other means the card and every fixture that claims to mirror it disagree about which labels scale, and the disagreement is invisible until a reader moves the servings control. The JS side is written as a regex LITERAL, not a quoted string, so the two texts are byte-comparable without normalising escapes.

twins.name: scaler-connector-set
twins.why: The closed set of connectors that make a label ONE amount written in parts: a plus sign, the word plus, a semicolon, and the word to. Added 2026-09-03 (queue 2026-09-02-corn06) to extend the compound-quantity rule to scaleBuy's third path, the plain leading-number one the 2026-09-01 fix deliberately left alone - which is how the estate came to hold the rule and its counter-example in the same function. TWO THINGS IN THIS TEXT ARE LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE RELAXED ON ONE SIDE ONLY. 'and' is absent: every 'and' label in the live corpus is a two-ingredient sentence ('About 1 tablespoon salt and 1 1/2 teaspoons black pepper'), not a two-portion sum. And 'to' demands whitespace on BOTH sides, so it cannot fire inside a word - 'cut into 1-inch cubes' is a knife cut, not a range, and nine of the fourteen must-not-move labels depend on exactly that.

twins.name: scaler-cook-unit-list
twins.why: The closed list of cook units a SECOND quantity must carry before it counts as another portion of the same amount. This list is the entire safety property of the connector path, measured label by label over all 7,838 live buy labels: 14 of the 71 multi-quantity labels carry a second number that must NEVER move - a knife cut ('cut into 1/2-inch pieces'), a can size ('3 1/2 14-oz cans'), a per-unit weight ('about 1/2 lb each'), a product name ('1/3-less-fat') or a cook time ('added the last 2 minutes') - and a general scale-every-number fix corrupts every one of them. Keep it CLOSED. 'minutes' in particular must never be added: it is the only token standing between the cheddar label and a scaled cook time. Widening it on one side only would move labels on the reader's card that no fixture on the other side can see.

twins.name: scaler-unit-vocabulary
twins.why: THE CLOSED SINGULAR/PLURAL TABLE the serving scaler re-agrees a unit noun against, added 2026-09-03 (queue 2026-09-03-539ff0) with the agreement itself. Until that day both twins re-derived the NUMBER and copied the tail through byte for byte, so a card rendered '2 cup grated' and '1 onion, diced' the moment a reader moved the servings control, and '1/2 cups' when a plural label scaled below one. Measured over all 7,838 live buy labels before the fix: 3,340 disagreeing renders across 328 labels and 564 recipes at f = 2 / 0.5 / 4 / 0.25, rising to 3,925 once every word the corpus actually carries in the unit slot is counted. WHAT IS ABSENT FROM THIS TEXT IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE ADDED ON ONE SIDE ONLY. Abbreviations are absent, so 'lb' and 'tbsp' stay invariant. Modifiers are absent, so '13 corn tortillas' cannot become '13 corns tortillas' and '10 sweet potatoes' cannot become '10 sweets potatoes'. And egg, breast, thigh, stick and bag are absent although the alert named them: not one of them leads the unit slot in any of the 1,365 distinct live labels, so an entry could never fire or be tested, and 'egg' is the likeliest noun-adjunct trap the day it does ('2 egg whites'). A word added to one side and not the other moves labels on the reader's card that no fixture on the other side can see.

twins.name: scaler-unit-leading-word
twins.why: WHICH WORD THE AGREEMENT ABOVE IS ALLOWED TO TOUCH: the first word of the tail, and nothing else. That restriction is the second half of the safety property, because the unit slot is the only place a label's noun is a function of its number - everything after it is a NOTE the writer put there. '3 1/2 cups shredded cheddar, added the last 2 minutes' must agree 'cups' and leave the rest alone, and '12 cloves garlic, minced' must agree 'cloves' and not 'garlic'. The lookahead refuses a hyphen as well as a letter so a hyphenated compound ('9 thick-cut slices') is not read as a bare unit noun. Relaxing the anchor on one side only would let the browser rewrite note text that no PowerShell fixture renders.

twins.name: whole-package-ceil-tolerance
twins.why: THE SLACK IN 'how many packages does this batch need', written down SEVEN times in two languages. You cannot buy 7.5 tbsp of vinegar, so every surface rounds up - but a batch needing 1005 g out of a 1000 g package should not be told to buy two, so the rule is ceil(x - 0.02) and the 2% is the deliberate part. Six copies carried 0.02 and two carried 1e-9 (costAt in the card widget and its PowerShell mirror Get-PkgCellCost), which rounds on floating-point noise instead. The card therefore printed one package MORE than its own Buy N line whenever a line landed inside that 2% window: 363 lines across 273 recipes the week it was found, 12 of them on the recipe's own package where a reader sees both numbers on one screen. Aligned to 0.02 on 2026-09-02 and declared here in the same commit. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING IT: this auditor compares TEXT, so what it pins is the CONSTANT. It cannot see the BASIS the numbers on either side of the minus sign are on - that is what let a gross gpu sit against drained grams for weeks with every twin green - and the basis is pinned instead by outcome: build-card2's fallback-package throw, wave-preaudit's widget-count-basis and compute-v2 -CrossCheck.
